propositions: Production in-process verifier (Arm A) achieved 100% per-AC agreement with ground truth on the corpus (65/65 ACs correct) with 0 false-PASS verdicts on planted-unmet ACs and 0 rejections on real ACs.

Minimal external-harness agent (Arm B) achieved 94.6% per-AC agreement (87/92 ACs correct) with 0 false-PASS verdicts but 5 false-FAIL rejections on real ACs, concentrated on epic AC7 and AC2 due to strict literal interpretation of coverage clauses.
Arm A median wall time was 131s while Arm B median was 415.5s (~3.2× slower), violating the predeclared rule that Arm B must be ≤2× Arm A's speed.
The predeclared GO decision rule required zero false-PASS (met), fewer rejections in Arm B than Arm A (failed: 5 vs 0), and Arm B wall time ≤2× Arm A (failed: 3.2× actual)—result NO-GO.
Zero INSUFFICIENT verdicts emerged from Arm B despite the hypothesis predicting insufficiency-loop pain; agents discovered the tickets branch and verified external-seeming ACs within the repository.

Operator hypothesis that unreliability lives in in-process scaffolding rather than the task itself was not supported; the control production verifier outperformed the minimal external harness on accuracy and speed.
